title: Optimization of blood pressure management after acute ischemic stroke and its prognostic significance: Prospective, randomized, open, blinded outcome evaluation, and feasibility Trial
author: Beom Joon Kim
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.9nqh5dw

steps.title: Screen Patients and Obtain Consent
steps.instruction: Identify patients with acute ischemic stroke and verify eligibility based on inclusion and exclusion criteria.

substeps.instruction: Confirm acute cerebral infarction via brain imaging within one week of onset.
Verify age is 19 years or older.
For pre-menopausal women or those within 1 year of menopause, confirm a negative Urine HCG test.
Ensure patient is stable enough to take prescribed blood pressure medications and can take oral drugs.
Verify that at least 24 hours have passed since the first recognition of stroke symptoms and the average systolic blood pressure (SBP) measured over the two days prior to registration is ≥ 135 mmHg.
Confirm the patient can use a Bluetooth-based blood pressure monitor and is expected to comply with visits and intervention plans.
Obtain signed informed consent from the patient.
Exclude patients who are pregnant, gave birth within 30 days, or are breastfeeding.
Exclude patients participating in other interventional trials or those transferring to nursing/rehabilitation hospitals.

Exclude patients with planned vascular or intracranial procedures (excluding carotid endarterectomy or stenting) during the 3-month trial, unless the procedure occurred before registration and the patient was stable for 48 hours.
Exclude patients with known hypersensitivity to Olmesartan, amlodipine, or hydrochlorothiazide.
Exclude patients with severe liver disease (e.g., ascites, coagulopathy) or renal failure requiring dialysis.

steps.title: Conduct Run-in Period
steps.instruction: Perform a run-in period for up to 14 days to stabilize blood pressure and train the patient on equipment.

substeps.instruction: Provide Olmesartan based on pre-inclusion average SBP: 20 mg if SBP ≤ 150 mmHg, or 40 mg if SBP > 150 mmHg.
Educate the patient on the use of the Bluetooth blood pressure monitor.
Install the synchronization application on the patient's smartphone and verify stable connectivity to the main server.
Ensure the patient can distinguish their own measurements using the device's identification buttons.
Monitor for screening failures: exclude patients who develop hypersensitivity, neurological deterioration, inability to use the Bluetooth monitor, or withdraw consent.

steps.title: Randomize Patients at Discharge
steps.instruction: Assign eligible patients to either the Intensive Management Group or the Control Group at the time of hospital discharge.

substeps.instruction: Perform stratified block randomization (1:1 ratio) by participating institution using SAS PROC PLAN.
Assign patients via the Interactive Web-based Response System (IWRS).
Provide comprehensive discharge education: smartphone app setup, BP measurement methods, medication adherence, and contact details for breakthrough visits.

steps.title: Implement Home Blood Pressure Monitoring
steps.instruction: Instruct all patients to measure blood pressure at home using the provided Bluetooth monitor according to a strict schedule.

substeps.instruction: Morning measurement: 15 minutes after waking, before eating, after 10 minutes of rest.
Evening measurement: 2 hours after dinner, after 10 minutes of rest.
Measurement technique: Sit comfortably in a quiet space with back and arm supported for 5 minutes before measuring.

Arm selection: Use the left arm for right-handed users and right arm for left-handed users; if the dominant arm is paralyzed, use the opposite arm. If the difference between arms is > 20 mmHg, use the arm with the higher reading.
Frequency: Measure twice per session (take the average) at least 5 days per week (total ≥ 10 measurements/week).

steps.title: Manage Intensive Management Group
steps.instruction: Apply the pharmacological algorithm and behavioral intensification for patients in the intensive group.

substeps.instruction: Target Blood Pressure: Office SBP < 140 mmHg; Home SBP 110-135 mmHg.
Behavioral Intervention: Send automated SMS if measurements are < 10/week; initiate nurse phone contact if measurements are < 6/week.
Clinical Intervention: Nurse phone contact if > 50% of measurements (minimum 6/week) are out of range (starting 2 weeks post-randomization). Schedule a breakthrough visit if clinically necessary.
Positive Reinforcement: Send congratulatory SMS if measurements are ≥ 10/week and all are within the target range.

Pharmacological Algorithm: 
- Step 1: Add amlodipine 5 mg (to Olmesartan 20 or 40 mg).
- Step 2: Increase amlodipine to 10 mg.
- Step 3: Add hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg.
- If still uncontrolled and Olmesartan is 20 mg, increase to 40 mg.
- If still uncontrolled after all steps, add other agents per investigator's judgment.
- If Home mean SBP < 110 mmHg, reduce doses or remove added drugs in reverse order.

steps.title: Manage Control Group
steps.instruction: Provide standard care for patients in the control group using Olmesartan-based therapy.

substeps.instruction: Provide Bluetooth monitors and training, but do not send automated SMS reminders or behavioral alerts.
Adjust medications at the 1-month visit based on the physician's discretion using Olmesartan 20 mg, amlodipine 5/10 mg, or hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg.
Reduce dosage if Home mean SBP < 110 mmHg.

steps.title: Perform Follow-up Visits
steps.instruction: Conduct scheduled and unscheduled visits to monitor safety, adherence, and efficacy.

substeps.instruction: Month 1 Visit (±10 days): Check BP, verify device function/data transmission, assess medication adherence, collect outcome variables, and record adverse events.
Month 3 Visit (±14 days): Repeat all Month 1 checks; conclude the study and transition to standard care.
Breakthrough/Unplanned Visits: Perform when triggered by the algorithm or patient request to assess BP, device function, adherence, and adjust medications.
